title: spec review: next_wave decision point v2: file the next wave when every execute child is merged or superseded and plan.md lists unfiled labels; closable accepts superseded children; capped relaunches; fail-safe plan parsing
spec:
Goal T-1403, plan label E12v2 (respec of T-1443 after spec review T-1462 request_changes; every risk is answered
below). Wave 1 of T-1403 finished 2026-10-01 09:30 and nothing happened for 8.5 h: no decision point covers
'filed work done, plan has more waves'.

Facts (goal/T-1403 after E9 T-1439; locate by symbol): planner_runs.decision_points() yields scouts_done, held and
closable only; closable needs every execute child merged_into, so a goal with superseded execute children never
closes (T-1403 has T-1405, T-1410, T-1413, T-1414 superseded). tick() routes each point through build_ctx() and
decision.route() (unknown kinds -> escalate 'unknown:kind'), then run_group(); run() and run_group() skip when
_session_attached(). daemon calls planner_runs.reconcile()/tick() only when [planner].autonomous is true (live
pool.toml false; harness forces false): leave that gate. _claim's decision_requested map and _condition_resolved()
are per kind; every non-'held' kind is goal-keyed in _decision_task, _observed_outcome, reconcile/jev and the
closable-only branches of build_ctx and tick (gate_state unknown, routine). planner_packet._KIND_FALLBACK maps
kinds to decision types; a missing entry falls to 'other'. Plan text lives in STATE/plan.md: section
'## GOAL <goal id> ...' up to the next '## ' line; wave lines start with 'Wave <n>'; additions are bullets
'- E3 (wave 3, ...) ...'. Filed children carry constraints.plan_label.

Change:
1. planner_runs.unfiled_labels(goal_id, children) -> sorted list. Labels = tokens matching
   (?<![\w./:-])[A-Z]\d{1,2}[a-z]?(?:v\d+)?(?![\w/:-]) on wave lines (^\s*(?:[-*]\s*)?Wave \d+\b) of the goal's
   section, plus the leading label of bullets ^\s*[-*]\s*<label>\s*\(wave \d+. Minus labels on lines starting
   'Dropped:' in that section. A label is filed when a child's plan_label equals it, or equals it followed by a
   lowercase letter or v<digits> (E11 -> E11a, A1 -> A1v2; A10 does NOT file A1). Fail safe (T-1462 #5): no
   plan.md, no section, OSError or UnicodeDecodeError -> []. Only the goal's section is read; the read happens
   only inside decision_points() for goals whose execute children are all merged_into or superseded (so the
   per-tick cost is zero for goals with queued/running work, T-1462 #6). Plan text is data: it yields only label
   tokens and never reaches a prompt except as those tokens.
2. decision_points(): for a goal with execute children where every execute child is merged_into or status
   'superseded', no child of any role is queued or running, no execute child is held, and unfiled_labels is
   non-empty -> yield (goal_id, 'next_wave', f"{goal_id}:{sha256(','.join(labels))[:12]}") unless _blocked; do not
   yield closable for that goal. CLOSABLE GAP DECIDED (T-1462 #2): closable now counts superseded execute children
   as resolved (every execute child merged_into OR superseded, same predicate as next_wave); with no unfiled
   labels a goal with superseded children becomes closable. Keep every existing closable test green by reading
   them first; test_closable_requires_every_execute_child_merged must still fail closable for a queued/held/done-
   unmerged child (only 'superseded' is newly accepted; adjust its fixture if it used superseded as the blocker).
3. next_wave in the goal-keyed paths (T-1462 #4): _decision_task returns the goal; _observed_outcome returns None
   for next_wave; tick() skips the closable-only gate_state/routine branches for next_wave; _record_running copies
   the point as [goal_id, payload_key] like closable. build_ctx: add unfiled_labels and goal_complexity.
   _claim decision_requested: 'file the next wave from plan.md'. _condition_resolved for next_wave: goal done, or
   the goal's current unfiled set hashes to a different key than the record's payload_key.
4. Retry and dedup (T-1462 #3): next_wave launches are capped PER GOAL across every payload_key: [planner].next_wave_max_launches (default 3, read with .get) bounds the number of next_wave decision runs launched for one goal (sum of attempts over the goal's next_wave records). At the cap, tick() launches nothing, notifies exactly once ('next_wave: Planner launched N times for <goal> without filing; edit plan.md, add a Dropped: line, or clear next_wave_capped') and writes next_wave_capped=true on the goal's newest next_wave record; a label-set change does NOT reset the cap, only clearing that field does. Each distinct key still follows the existing attempts/gave_up rule of _claim/reconcile.
5. decision.route(): kind next_wave -> required field unfiled_labels checked by key presence (an empty list is
   valid, T-1462 #6): missing -> escalate 'unknown:unfiled_labels'; empty -> none 'no_unfiled_work'; else escalate
   'next_wave_unfiled' (planner_router picks the tier). Add unfiled_labels to the evidence fields.
6. planner_packet._KIND_FALLBACK gains next_wave -> 'other' explicitly, with a comment, and the packet includes
   unfiled_labels in the goal section so the decision Planner reads them (planner_packet.py joins scope, T-1462
   #4, #7).
7. .orchestrator/prompts/planner-decision.md: one sentence: a next_wave decision means every filed execute task of
   the goal is merged or superseded while plan.md still lists unfiled labels; file the next wave from plan.md (SPEC
   RULE, depends_on by plan label) or record under 'Needs the human' why not, and list labels that will never be
   filed on a 'Dropped:' line.

Tests that assert the old behaviour (SPEC RULE): tests/test_planner_runs.py::test_closable_requires_every_execute_child_merged
and test_decision_points_scouts_done_held_closable write no plan.md and must pass (adjust only as rule 2 says);
tests/test_decision.py::test_disabled_routes_everything_to_escalate and the unknown-field table must pass
unchanged; tests/test_planner_taxonomy.py: next_wave classifies as decision_type 'other' (do not edit
planner_taxonomy.py); tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py and tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py must pass.

Depends on E9 (merged). The human decides when [planner].autonomous goes true. Rollback (T-1462 #8): `git revert`
of the merge commit; existing next_wave records stay inert because decision_points() no longer yields the kind;
the Planner records it in decisions.md at merge.

Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1403. Commit first, then run the focused tests in the foreground; never background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests. Locate every insertion point by symbol, never by the line numbers quoted here.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_runs.py::test_next_wave_point_when_filed_work_resolved_and_plan_lists_unfiled_labels: passes: with STATE/plan.md holding a '## GOAL <id>' section whose wave lines name A1, A2, B1 and children plan_label A1 (merged) and A2 (superseded), decision_points() yields (goal, 'next_wave', key) and not closable; nothing is yielded while any child is queued/running or an execute child is held, or once B1 is filed (or listed on a 'Dropped:' line); a goal whose execute children are all merged or superseded with no unfiled labels yields closable; tick() records a skip and launches nothing while _session_attached() is true, and launches exactly one decision run for a next_wave point with route escalate when detached (launcher patched)

tests/test_planner_runs.py::test_unfiled_labels_fails_safe_and_matches_suffixes: passes: unfiled_labels returns [] with no plan.md, no goal section, an unreadable file (OSError patched) and a non-UTF-8 file; a wave line whose prose contains 'B1' only inside a path-like or word token is not a label; 'Dropped: B9' removes B9; E11 is filed by plan_label E11a and A1 by A1v2 but A1 is not filed by A10; after [planner].next_wave_max_launches launches without filing, tick() notifies once and launches nothing until the record is cleared

tests/test_decision.py::test_next_wave_routes_escalate_or_none: passes: decision.route on kind next_wave returns escalate 'next_wave_unfiled' with unfiled_labels in the evidence when the list is non-empty, none 'no_unfiled_work' when the list is present but empty, and escalate 'unknown:unfiled_labels' when the field is missing
tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py::test_next_wave_packet_lists_unfiled_labels: passes: the packet for a next_wave point maps to decision type 'other' and its goal section lists the unfiled labels

risks.issue: Rule 2 makes superseded execute children count as resolved for closable. But build_ctx still sets all_children_merged = all(status == 'done' and merged_into), and routine_close (~line 1547) refuses unless all_children_merged. A goal like T-1403 would therefore yield closable and then route 'escalate children_unmerged' in decision.route. It would launch a Planner and never close routinely, so the stated closable gap is only half fixed. The spec lists neither build_ctx's closable branch nor the routine_close guard.

The cap uses next_wave_capped on the newest next_wave record, and only clearing that field resets it. Nothing in the spec says who clears it or how. A manual edit of the records file is the only path, and the 'edit plan.md or add Dropped:' remedy in the notification does not reset it. It is also unclear whether a goal's later, genuinely new waves stay blocked forever. This is state that never decreases. It needs an auto-reset when a launch results in a filed child (unfiled set shrinks), or a documented clear command.

The cap sums attempts over all of a goal's next_wave records. _claim/reconcile attempts are incremented on exited_early and failed_launch, and the spec does not say whether a successful exited_ok launch counts. 'Number of runs launched' and 'attempts' can diverge: a run that exits_ok without filing might count as 0, or each retry might count twice. State exactly which counter is summed, and where the cap check sits relative to _claim, so a launch is not double counted.

_condition_resolved for next_wave recomputes unfiled_labels, which re-reads plan.md. Under the fail-safe, [] on an OSError makes the unfiled set hash differently, so the condition reads as resolved. A transient read failure could clear or mark a running record resolved and permit a relaunch with a new key. Specify that a read failure is not 'resolved' (distinguish unreadable from empty), or that the empty-set hash is excluded.

The goal section is bounded by the next '## ' line, but plan.md is also written by the Planner (untrusted-adjacent) and wave lines are free prose. The label regex will pick up labels in unrelated wave lines, for example 'Wave 2 depends on E9 (merged)', so a label the plan merely mentions as done or external becomes 'unfiled' and drives repeated launches until the cap. The spec has only the Dropped: escape hatch. Consider restricting to labels introduced on the line (e.g. before ':' or '-') or require a test for the 'mentions merged label' case.

tick() has a legacy branch ('routes' not in config) that calls run() for the first point only. The spec's acceptance tests do not say which config path they exercise, and next_wave in run() uses the same _claim/decision_requested paths with route=None. The spec does not say that the cap and notify logic must live where both tick paths reach it.

suggested_spec_changes: Add to rule 2/3: build_ctx closable branch computes all_children_merged with the same predicate as decision_points (every execute child merged_into OR status 'superseded'), and routine_close's guard uses it. Add a test that a goal with merged plus superseded children and no unfiled labels routes closable to 'routine' (green gate), not 'children_unmerged'. Alternatively, state that these goals intentionally escalate and say why.
Define how next_wave_capped is cleared: auto-clear it when the goal's unfiled set strictly shrinks or a new child is filed. Or name the supported command or edit that does it, and test it.
State precisely which counter next_wave_max_launches sums (launches[] length vs attempts) and place the cap check inside the lock/claim path so the count and the launch are atomic.

Specify that unfiled_labels failures (OSError/decode/no section) in _condition_resolved are treated as 'unknown, not resolved', and in decision_points as 'no point'. Add a test for the running-record case.
Name which tick path (routes configured or legacy) the tick acceptance tests use, and require the cap in both, or state that legacy is out of scope.
